_comment: English bodies for metagpt (framework). Mechanism per C0-1..6. No extraSections in source; sections/sectionTitles omitted. providers not rendered — not included.

axes.model_access: Multi-model access (each vendor's API and local lines, not itemized); its narrative is not the model but "writing a software company's process into multi-agent collaboration" (official repo description: "The Multi-Agent Framework: First AI Software Company").
axes.runtime: A Python multi-agent framework: a role pipeline of "product manager → architect → engineer → QA" collaborates to produce software artifacts. GitHub FoundationAgents/MetaGPT 71,097 stars (API verified); **last push 2026-01-21, latest release v0.8.2 (2025-03-09)** — mainline repo updates clearly slowed (other org repos remain active, see pitfalls).
axes.local_files: Runs locally: install via pip and it executes on your own machine; generated code, documents and temp artifacts all land in your working directory; there is no cloud-runs-it-for-you hosted execution line (the official docs offer no hosted surface).
axes.background: Batch-style pipelines are the main mode (one task runs through one software-production pipeline), not a resident message-receiving form; the research line is active (org repos such as CEO-Arena still pushing in 2026-10).
axes.tools: Built-in role-action / code-execution / document-output tool lines; MCP support status not itemized.
axes.context: Encoding SOPs (standard operating procedures) into role interactions is its core design — context is organized as inter-role messaging (per the official docs).
axes.permissions: Code execution happens on your machine; intermediate artifacts of a fully automatic multi-agent pipeline should be human-reviewed before landing — the output quality and responsibility surface of a fully automatic "software company" sits with the user.
axes.fit: Fits: multi-agent collaboration research, SOP pipeline experiments, academic reproduction of the software-generation process (heavily cited paper line). Does not fit: production selections needing active maintenance (pushes/releases slowed), fine-grained single-agent control.

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/framework/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/framework/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- MCP support status (not itemized)
- Whether the mainline has moved into a "research-maintenance only" state (not stated officially; recorded as maintenance per push/release facts, no assertion made)
- The relationship between DeepWisdom's commercial product line and the framework (not verified)
related: Same-category contrast: both are multi-role collaboration frameworks — CrewAI targets production orchestration and releases actively, MetaGPT leans to research pipelines and its repo has slowed; activity is the selection gap.

Same-category contrast: both are China-origin multi-agent frameworks — AgentScope (Alibaba line) is still pushing actively while MetaGPT's repo has slowed; even within the China-origin line there is an active/slow split.

Cross-category contrast: Devin is a finished product that works for you (coding category); MetaGPT is a base for you to build a "software-company pipeline" (framework category) — the two sides of the §7 inclusion standard.
